Q: AADSTS70002: Error validating credentials. AADSTS50126: Invalid username or password A:

For me the below worked out in Postman.

URL(POST) :

https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant_id>/oauth2/v2.0/token

Header:

Content-Type 
application/x-www-form-urlencoded

Request Body(text):

client_id=<client_id>&
scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default&
grant_type=client_credentials&
client_secret=<client_secret>

Q: Angular 6 - display component as modal dialog from a component.ts A:

Most people would put this code inside the parent's submit method:

this.modalRef = this.modalService.open(ConfirmationModal, { centered: true, 
    size: 'sm' });

Notice the use of ConfirmationModal in above code.

You would also need to move the close logic to the parent.

However, I can see that you are trying to go for something more reusable.

What you need to do is call the open method from your home.component

To call a child method in a parent/child relationship is easy using @ViewChild

Docs are here: https://angular.io/guide/component-interaction#parent-calls-an-viewchild

However, I'm not sure this is a parent/child relationship so I'm not sure how much success you will have. You may be forced to fall back to putting the code inside the parent's submit method. Let me know if you find another way, I would be interested to hear.

Q: Python tkinter wait_window does not return A:

wait_window() itself isn't what stands out as the problem here.

Its job is to start a nested Tk event loop and block until the window is destroyed. Once destroy() is called, wait_window() returns and execution continues. That's exactly what it's intended to do for modal dialogs.

With your controller code:

self._connect_view = ConnectView(self._view)
print("IP " + self._connect_view.get_ip())

the expected flow is:

  1. ConnectView is created.

  2. wait_window() blocks while the dialog is open.

  3. The user clicks Connect.

  4. ok() saves the value from the entry.

  5. cancel() calls destroy().

  6. wait_window() returns.

  7. print() executes.

So that part looks fine.

What does stand out is this code in MainView:

if observable.isinstance(ChatModel):

isinstance is a built-in function, not a method of an object. It should be:

if isinstance(observable, ChatModel):

If update_observer() is called, the current code will raise an AttributeError. If you're running from an IDE that doesn't show the traceback, it can easily look like the application has just frozen.

I'd also move wait_window() out of the dialog constructor. Having a constructor block until the window closes is unusual and makes the class less reusable. A more common pattern is:

dialog = ConnectView(self._view)
dialog.wait_window()
print(dialog.get_ip())

and remove:

self.wait_window()

from ConnectView.__init__().

One more thing I'd add is:

self.transient(parent)
self.grab_set()

before calling wait_window(). grab_set() makes the dialog modal, and transient() makes it behave like a child of the main window (stays on top, minimizes with the parent, etc.).

If the button remains visually pressed and nothing happens, I'd suspect an exception in one of the callbacks rather than wait_window() itself. Running the program from a terminal instead of the IDE is a good way to check, since any traceback will be printed there.

Q: Convert a hmmer --tblout output to a pandas dataframe A: 
import pandas as pd
new_header = ["target_name","target_accession","tlen","query_name","query_accession","qlen","seq_E-value","seq_score","seq_bias","dom_#","dom_of","dom_c-Evalue","dom_i-Evalue","dom_score","dom_bias","hmm_from","hmm_to","ali_from","ali_to","env_from","env_to","acc","description_of_target"]
hmm_res = pd.read_csv("hmmsearch.domtblout", sep=r"\s+", comment="#", header=None, index_col=None, names=new_header, engine="python", usecols=list(range(0, 23)))

This will parse the domain table into pandas dataframe.

If you use spaces in the names of the sequences then this approach will fail, because pandas will try to create extra columns. The usecols parameter helps when annotations in description_of_target have spaces, but it will truncate the annotations to the space.
